0.long_answer: Leber congenital amaurosis (LCA) is an inherited eye disease first described by the German ophthalmologist Theodor von Leber in 1869. LCA is a severe retinal dystrophy that manifests with profound visual loss at birth or in early childhood. It is characterized by symptoms such as nystagmus, sluggish pupillary responses, and pigmentary retinopathy. The condition is most often inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern and is considered one of the earliest and most severe forms of inherited retinal dystrophies, accounting for a significant proportion of congenital blindness in children.
